findings.summary: `loom-pr-merge-gate` still needs final live GitHub readback after this review record is pushed: workflow run on PR head, branch protection or ruleset requiring the stable check name, and controlled-merge consumption of that required-check readback.

disposition.summary: Collect and record final host readback proof after pushing this review record.

findings.details: Host enforcement truth lives outside the repository tree, so it must be proven after CI sees the final PR head.

findings.summary: The required check workflow checks out and executes repository code from the PR head. This preserves head binding, but it remains a host-trust decision for repositories that accept untrusted external PRs.

disposition.summary: Documented as a governance boundary; repositories can restrict contributors or replace the workflow body with pinned tooling/API-fetched artifacts before requiring the check.

findings.details: The workflow uses read-scoped permissions, but required-check execution of PR-supplied code remains an explicit trust boundary.

findings.summary: The stock workflow currently targets direct PR merges via `pull_request`; repositories that enable GitHub merge queue must explicitly add and validate `merge_group` support.

disposition.summary: Keep merge-queue support out of WI-763 direct PR merge scope unless Loom self-governance enables merge queue.

findings.details: Current Loom self-governance uses direct PR merge; merge queue compatibility remains a documented follow-up decision.
